title: Connected components of algebraic spaces over separably closed fields
statement: Let $k$ be a separably closed field [def-weil-field, def-pc-separably-closed], let $L/k$ be any field extension [def-pc-field-extension], and let $Z$ be an algebraic space over $\operatorname{Spec}k$ [def-trf-algebraic-space, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Give point spaces their atlas topology [def-a1-space-point-topology], and use sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. A connected component is a maximal nonempty connected subset, and connected means nonempty and admitting no partition into two nonempty relatively open subsets. Put $Z_L=Z\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}L$ and let $p:Z_L\to Z$ be the projection. Then $|p|$ is continuous, surjective and open. Inverse image under $|p|$ gives a bijection from the connected components of $|Z|$ to the connected components of $|Z_L|$. A component $D\subseteq |Z|$ is open and closed if and only if $|p|^{-1}(D)$ is open and closed. Consequently every open-and-closed component $C\subseteq Z_L$ is uniquely of the form $D\times_kL$ for an open-and-closed component subspace $D\subseteq Z$, with open-subspace structures [def-a1-space-open-subspace]. In particular, $Z$ is connected if and only if it is geometrically connected over $k$, where the latter means that $Z_{k'}$ is connected for every field extension $k'/k$. No quasi-compactness or finite type hypothesis on $Z$, or algebraicity hypothesis on $L/k$, is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0A12, lemma-separably-closed-field-connected-components. proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-space-over-field-universally-open] with $X=\operatorname{Spec}L$ and $Y=Z$: its projection is $p$, so $|p|$ is open. By [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus], $|p|$ is continuous. These inputs allow arbitrary algebraic spaces and arbitrary field extensions; no finite-presentation argument is being used.

source.place: Tag 0A12 via lemma-bijection-connected-components; openness is Tag 06DN.

proof.text: The scheme $\operatorname{Spec}L$ is nonempty and connected: a field has exactly one prime ideal, $(0)$. Apply [lem-weil-separably-closed-geometrically-connected] over the separably closed field $k$. Thus $\operatorname{Spec}L$ is geometrically connected over $k$, and for every field extension $K/k$ the scheme $\operatorname{Spec}L\times_k\operatorname{Spec}K$ is nonempty and connected.

source.place: Tag 0A12, first two sentences; the scheme input is varieties.tex Tag 0363.

proof.text: For $z\in|Z|$, choose a representative $\operatorname{Spec}K\to Z$. The point-image formula of [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus], applied to $Z_L\to Z$ and this representative, says that the image of $|Z_L\times_Z\operatorname{Spec}K|$ in $|Z_L|$ is exactly $|p|^{-1}(\{z\})$. The sheaf pullback universal property [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] identifies this source with $\operatorname{Spec}L\times_k\operatorname{Spec}K$: on every test scheme both functors are the same compatible pairs. It is connected and nonempty by step 2. Its continuous image is therefore connected and nonempty: a separation of the image would pull back to a separation of the source. This proves that every fibre of $|p|$ is connected, and also proves surjectivity.

source.place: lemma-bijection-connected-components, fibre-image paragraph, using spaces-properties.tex Tag 03H4.

proof.text: The open continuous surjection $|p|$ has the quotient topology: for every subset $A\subseteq|Z|$, if $|p|^{-1}(A)$ is closed, then $|Z|\setminus A=|p|(|Z_L|\setminus|p|^{-1}(A))$ is open; the converse is continuity. Apply [lem-sfb-quotient-connected-component-preimage] to obtain $|p|^{-1}(\operatorname{Comp}_{|Z|}(p(x)))=\operatorname{Comp}_{|Z_L|}(x)$ for every $x$. Given a component $D$, choose $z\in D$ and a lift $x$; this equality makes its inverse image a component. Every component upstairs contains some $x$, so occurs this way; surjectivity makes inverse image injective on subsets. This is the required bijection. If $Z$ is empty, both component sets are empty and the assertions are vacuous.

For any subset $D\subseteq|Z|$, continuity carries clopenness to its inverse image. Conversely, if $|p|^{-1}(D)$ is clopen, openness and surjectivity give $D=|p|(|p|^{-1}(D))$ and $|Z|\setminus D=|p|(|p|^{-1}(|Z|\setminus D))$ open. Hence $D$ is clopen. This applies in particular to the corresponding components of step 4.

source.place: Tag 0A12, clopen refinement of the open-surjection proof.

proof.text: Let $C$ be a clopen component upstairs and let $D\subseteq|Z|$ be the unique corresponding component from step 4. Step 5 makes $D$ clopen. By [lem-a1-space-etale-open-image], its open subset has a unique open subspace structure. By [lem-a1-space-open-factor-scheme-tests], the open subspace $D\times_kL\subseteq Z_L$ has point image $|p|^{-1}(D)=|C|$. The inclusion-preserving bijection between open subspaces and open subsets in [lem-a1-space-etale-open-image] identifies it with $C$. The same bijection, together with injectivity of inverse image on subsets, proves uniqueness of the open component subspace $D$.

source.place: Tag 03BZ, lemma-open-subspaces; Tag 03IE, lemma-factor-through-open-subspace, with the pullback point-image formula.

proof.text: If $Z$ is connected, it is nonempty and its only connected component is $|Z|$. Step 4, for every extension $k\subseteq k'$, makes $|Z_{k'}|$ its only component; it is nonempty by surjectivity. Thus $Z$ is geometrically connected. Conversely use the identity field extension in the definition of geometric connectedness. The empty space satisfies neither connectedness convention.

Step 6: etale-open-image gives the bijection between open subspaces and open subsets, and the last clause of open-factor-scheme-tests gives the point image of J x_Z Z_L; uniqueness follows by injectivity.
